newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Coast says Q2 hurt by higher tax.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Coast says Q2 hurt by higher tax.

text.p: Atlantic Coast Airlines said Wednesday its higher tax rate for the second quarter, compared to 1996, hurt its net income per share by $0.36.
The company reported fully diluted earnings per share of $0.65 compared to $0.94 for the same year-earlier period.

The company said its net income for the second quarter reflects a full provision for income taxes based on a 39 percent effective tax rate, as compared to a 5 percent tax rate in the second quarter of 1996.
As of December 31, 1996, the company used its remaining net operating losses for tax purposes.
The company also said its lower yields in the second quarter on a year-over-year basis was the result of the airline ticket tax being in effect during that quarter.

Its second quarter operations resulted in a 7.2 percent increase in total passengers carried and a 9 percent increase in revenue passenger miles. Available seat miles increased 6 percent, while its load factor increased by 1.4 load factor points.
